newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian nickel, tin seen gaining in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian nickel, tin seen gaining in quiet trade.

text.p: Indian nickel and tin prices are expected to gain in the next few days on the back of an uptrend on the London Metal Exchange (LME), dealers said on Wednesday.
"Nickel and tin will be active in the Indian market, which otherwise is expected to remain quiet next week," said Bombay Metal Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
Parikh said nickel and tin firmed in line with rising prices on the LME, where the two metals gained $600 and $100 per tonne respectively in the last three days.
"There's no genuine demand for nickel and tin," Parikh said. "It's just that traders are stocking the metals in anticipation of a further rise in their prices."
Parikh said the state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd and Hindustan Zinc Ltd would announce their August prices in the next few days.
"The market will remain quiet till the new prices come into force," he said.
Traders said aluminium prices could also strengthen on a firm global trend and increasing domestic demand.
In the week to Wednesday, nickel rose 1,100 rupees to 34,300 rupees per quintal and tin added 700 rupees to 29,200 rupees per quintal.
Aluminium gained 100 rupees to 7,800 rupees per quintal and zinc made a similar gain at 8,400 rupees per quintal. Lead was up 50 rupees at 4,200 rupees per quintal.
